title: CJP Founder Dipke Begins Hunger Strike After Wangchuk Moved to Hospital
excerpt: Abhijeet Dipke announced an indefinite hunger strike hours after Delhi Police shifted Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital on his 21st day of fasting, escalating the protest demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Abhijeet Dipke begins an indefinite hunger strike after Sonam Wangchuk's hospitalization.
  • Wangchuk lost over 8 kg during his 20-day fast, risking organ failure.
  • CJP demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over NEET exam irregularities.
  • A march to Parliament is planned for July 20 to amplify their demands.
  • Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke announced an indefinite hunger strike on Saturday after police moved Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital from the Jantar Mantar protest site.
  • Wangchuk, 59, had been fasting for 20 days and lost over 8 kg; doctors warned of organ failure risk before police intervened citing a Delhi High Court order.
  • The CJP is demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak and exam irregularities that affected millions of students.
  • Protesters plan a march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session, to press their demands.

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke declared an indefinite hunger strike on Saturday, hours after Delhi Police shifted climate activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital from the protest site at Jantar Mantar.

"I am starting an indefinite hunger strike beginning right now," Dipke, 30, wrote in a post on X. The announcement came after police arrived at the protest site early Saturday morning and moved the ailing Wangchuk amid sloganeering and resistance from CJP supporters.

Wangchuk Hospitalized After 20 Days of Fasting

Wangchuk, 59, had been on an indefinite hunger strike since June 28, consuming only water while demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination. By Saturday, he had been fasting for 20 days and lost more than 8 kg, dropping to roughly 57 kg.

The Delhi High Court on Thursday had directed authorities to conduct daily clinical health assessments of Wangchuk, observing that "the life of any citizen is precious" and instructing the Centre to ensure all necessary medical intervention. The court order came in response to a public interest litigation filed by advocate Rakesh Kumar Saini, who argued Wangchuk's deteriorating health had become "life-threatening" and sought directions for force-feeding if necessary.

Doctors monitoring Wangchuk on Friday described his condition as an emergency, expressing concern over possible organ failure.

"As per orders of Hon'ble High Court and on expert medical advise due to the deteriorating health condition of Sh. Sonam Wangchuk, he has been shifted to the hospital for essential medical care."

- Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi), statement on X

The DCP's statement also noted that "protestors tried to create obstruction, in which slight commotion ensued," and asked demonstrators at Jantar Mantar to "peacefully vacate the place at the earliest."

A Movement Born Online, Tested on the Streets

The CJP protest at Jantar Mantar began on June 20 amid the NEET paper leak controversy that affected millions of students. The party, founded by Dipke, gained 22 million Instagram followers within days of its launch in May and has become a rare focal point of youth-led defiance against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, according to Reuters.

Wangchuk joined the protest on June 28, launching the hunger strike alongside six students from the All India Students' Association (AISA). On the third day of his fast, he told Reuters the strike could last six weeks unless he died first. "A sensitive government in a democracy listens to the pains of the people, and I hope they will take action," he said.

Over the past three weeks, several opposition leaders visited the protest site. Congress leader Pawan Khera, Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav, former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, and BKU leader Rakesh Tikait — who arrived with 500 farmers on July 17 — all expressed support. Actor Aamir Khan, speaking at the London Indian Film Festival on Friday, said he was "concerned about Sonam Wangchuk's health" and urged him to end the fast.

March to Parliament Planned for July 20

The CJP has called for a march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session, to press for Pradhan's resignation and broader exam reforms. Dipke earlier wrote an open letter to Prime Minister Modi, asking: "How long will your government choose to ignore our voices, sir?"

"We have been trying to convince Sonam sir to withdraw his hunger strike but he is adamant to continue it. Sonam sir is asking us to keep preparing for the march to parliament on 20th July. I feel the government wants Sonam sir and other people on hunger strike to die."

- Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder, to Reuters

Wangchuk spent roughly six months in jail last year after Modi's government accused him of inciting violence during protests in the Himalayan territory of Ladakh — charges he denied. He was released in March 2026.

What Comes Next

With Wangchuk now hospitalized and Dipke taking over the fast, the protest enters an unpredictable phase. Pradhan, his ministry, and the government's chief spokesperson have not publicly responded to the CJP's demands. The Delhi High Court is expected to take up the matter again in a scheduled hearing. Whether the July 20 march draws the kind of turnout the CJP hopes for will test whether a movement that exploded online can sustain pressure on the streets.
